title: One question, four analytical approaches
caption: Illustrative retail scenario. Observational diagnostics alone do not establish causation.
alt: Illustrative retail scenario. Observational diagnostics alone do not establish causation.
question: Can an association prove why orders fell?
answer: No. A causal claim requires a suitable design and assumptions.

title: Retail analytics pipeline
caption: Immutable raw records support traceability; validated facts and dimensions feed the semantic model. Failed records are reviewed.
alt: Three sources feed ingestion, immutable storage, transformation, curated tables, Power BI and a report; a quarantine branch reprocesses corrections.
question: Why keep the raw layer?
answer: To preserve provenance and enable reproducible reprocessing.

title: ETL versus ELT: transformation location
caption: Same retail operational database and analytics warehouse in both. ETL transforms before loading; ELT loads raw then transforms inside the target. Both require governance and can retain raw history.
alt: Two parallel data paths: ETL extraction, staging transformation outside the warehouse, and curated load; ELT extraction, raw warehouse load, and transformation within the warehouse. Amber and location labels identify transformation.
question: Can ETL retain raw history?
answer: Yes. It can archive extracts before transformation; neither approach is universally superior.

title: One order in three representations
caption: Representation affects parsing; CSV does not provide native types or a relational constraint system.
alt: Representation affects parsing; CSV does not provide native types or a relational constraint system.
question: Does CSV enforce a unique key?
answer: No. The reader must validate uniqueness.

title: Business framing before analysis
caption: Define metric, denominator, time window, stakeholder, and decision before choosing a chart.
alt: Define metric, denominator, time window, stakeholder, and decision before choosing a chart.
question: Why not average row margins?
answer: That weights small and large sales equally; portfolio margin is a ratio of totals.

title: Before and after data cleaning
caption: Eight synthetic raw records become six accepted transactions. The exact duplicate is removed, negative quantity quarantined, missing quantity imputed to 3 with its indicator retained, and the verified 50,000 USD sale kept.
alt: Before table flags duplicate row 8, missing quantity in row 3, North spelling in row 2, and negative quantity in row 4. Clean table retains six transactions and a True missing flag for S03; the decision log explains each choice.
question: Why is S06 retained despite its unusually large revenue?
answer: Its quantity and price were verified as valid. A statistical extreme alone is not an error.

title: MCAR, MAR and MNAR income reporting
caption: Illustrative patient-income mechanisms, not diagnoses. MCAR is random loss independent of age/income; MAR depends on observed age and not income conditional on age; MNAR still depends on unreported income after conditioning.
alt: Three reporting diagrams: random loss causes missing income; observed age predicts reporting under MAR; true unreported income predicts reporting under MNAR even after observed age is accounted for. A heatmap cannot prove MAR versus MNAR.
question: Does missingness varying by age prove MAR?
answer: No. It can contradict MCAR, but MNAR may remain possible because unreported income is unobserved.

title: Mean, median, fences and whiskers
caption: Exact synthetic values: [10,12,13,14,15], then append 100. Mean changes from 12.8 to 82/3; median from 13 to 13.5. Quartiles use linear percentiles; the fence thresholds are not whisker endpoints.
alt: Mean/median comparison shows mean 12.8 then 27.3333 and median 13 then 13.5. Augmented boxplot has Q1 12.25, Q3 14.75, fences 8.5/18.5, actual whiskers 10/15, and outlier 100.
question: Does the upper whisker end at 18.5?
answer: No. 18.5 is the upper fence; the whisker ends at the largest observed value inside it, 15.

title: Scaling and transforming the same values
caption: Exact values [10,20,30,40,100]. Min–max uses 10 and 100; standardization uses mean 40 and population SD 10√10 (ddof=0); log1p uses natural logarithms. Decimals are rounded to six places beside exact expressions.
alt: Table maps five original values to exact min–max fractions, standardized multiples of 1/√10 and natural logs of x+1. Aligned dot plots show standardization preserves relative spacing and distribution shape.
question: Does standardization make the data normally distributed?
answer: No. It shifts and rescales values using a positive affine transformation, preserving shape.

title: An unseen scaled value can exceed one
caption: Fit min–max on training values from 10 to 100, then transform 120 unchanged. The result is (120−10)/90 = 11/9, approximately 1.222222. Clipping is disabled.
alt: Training minimum 10 and maximum 100 define (x−10)/90. An arrow applies this fixed formula to unseen x=120, yielding 11/9 greater than one; refitting on test values is marked leakage.
question: Should the scaler be refitted to force 120 into the unit interval?
answer: No. Preserve the training-fitted parameters. Optional clipping hides the extent beyond the fitted range.

title: Ordered severity and unordered regions
caption: Severity explicitly maps Low < Medium < High to 0,1,2. Region membership is represented by four one-hot columns. Ordinal rank does not establish equal distances between severity levels.
alt: Two connected tables encode Low/Medium/High as 0/1/2 and North/South/East/West as one-hot membership rows. Arbitrary region integers can introduce an unintended order or distance.
question: Why can North=0, South=1, East=2, West=3 be misleading?
answer: A model may interpret numerical order or distance although the regions are unordered.

title: A transaction becomes useful features
caption: Synthetic transaction: quantity 3, price 200 USD/unit, discount 0.10, cost 120 USD/unit; assumed date 2024-01-08. Gross 600 USD, net 540, cost 360, profit 180, margin 1/3; month 1 and weekday 0 (Monday).
alt: Raw-field table points to formula/result table computing revenue, cost, profit, margin and date features. A caution excludes final profit, future sales and later returns from earlier predictions.
question: Can final realized profit predict an outcome before the sale is complete?
answer: Only if it was actually available at that prediction time; otherwise it is a future-derived leakage feature.

title: Choose a split for the data structure
caption: Synthetic 12-record schematics use nine training and three test records. Random suits independent records; stratification approximates class proportions; grouping isolates patients; chronological splitting holds out later dates.
alt: Four labeled split patterns: random record assignment, class-proportion preserving assignment, all three records of patient P4 held out, and October–December held out after January–September training. Color and hatching identify partitions.
question: Does stratification prevent repeated-patient leakage?
answer: No. Group splitting is needed to keep a patient entirely in one partition.

title: A safe predictive workflow
caption: Split first. During tuning, fit preprocessing within each training fold; transform its validation fold separately. Select the recipe, refit on all training data, transform test with training-fitted preprocessing and evaluate once.
alt: Training-side validation loop selects preprocessing/model settings before final refitting. Test remains untouched until final transformation/evaluation. Red dashed arrows mark test-data fitting and future-derived features as leakage.
question: When must a scaler be fitted during cross-validation?
answer: Inside each fold using only that fold’s training partition; final refitting uses all training data after recipe selection.

title: Underfitting, appropriate capacity and overfitting
caption: Reproducible synthetic regression, seed 42: y=0.7x²−0.5x+1 plus noise SD 0.65. Prespecified polynomial degrees 1,2,15 share 24 training observations and 400 independent held-out observations. MSE values are calculated; extreme curve segments outside the stated axis are clipped.
alt: Three panels show identical training points with linear, quadratic and degree-15 polynomial fits. Training MSE: 4.3248, 0.2815, 0.0829; held-out MSE: 4.1442, 0.4425, 0.6539. The quadratic generalizes best in this stated example.
question: Why is the smallest training error not the strongest evidence of generalization?
answer: A flexible model can fit training noise. Here degree 15 reduces training MSE but has larger held-out MSE than degree 2.

title: Shape is more than mean and SD
caption: Synthetic samples, seed 11. Mean–median–mode ordering is not a universal theorem; a symmetric distribution can have two modes.
alt: Synthetic samples, seed 11. Mean–median–mode ordering is not a universal theorem; a symmetric distribution can have two modes.
question: Does symmetry guarantee a unique mode?
answer: No. The bimodal example has two peaks.

title: Same center, different spread
caption: Exact samples: narrow [-2,-1,0,1,2]; wide [-6,-3,0,3,6]. Population SD; linear-interpolated quartiles.
alt: Exact samples: narrow [-2,-1,0,1,2]; wide [-6,-3,0,3,6]. Population SD; linear-interpolated quartiles.
question: Can equal means imply equal variability?
answer: No.

title: Association depends on relationship shape
caption: Synthetic examples, seed 12. A near-zero Pearson coefficient does not rule out a nonlinear association. Neither coefficient proves causation.
alt: Synthetic examples, seed 12. A near-zero Pearson coefficient does not rule out a nonlinear association. Neither coefficient proves causation.
question: Why is the U-shape correlation weak?
answer: Positive and negative slopes cancel in a linear summary.

title: Choose the question before the test
caption: A normality test alone does not choose the method. The design and estimand determine interpretation.
alt: A normality test alone does not choose the method. The design and estimand determine interpretation.
question: What does Mann–Whitney generally compare?
answer: Distributions/ranks; a location interpretation needs additional assumptions.

title: Split, aggregate, and change layout
caption: Synthetic six-row example. North=180, South=140; grand total=320. Pivot totals reconcile to raw revenue.
alt: Synthetic six-row example. North=180, South=140; grand total=320. Pivot totals reconcile to raw revenue.
question: What is the pivot grand total?

title: Time-series components and smoothing
caption: Synthetic 36 months, seed 14. Known construction: trend + annual seasonality + noise. This does not prove such components exist in arbitrary real data.
alt: Synthetic 36 months, seed 14. Known construction: trend + annual seasonality + noise. This does not prove such components exist in arbitrary real data.
question: Why are the first two full-window averages absent?
answer: Three observations are required for a complete trailing window.

title: EDA answers questions with limitations
caption: Generated synthetic accidents, seed 399. Counts lack traffic exposure and reporting denominators, so they do not establish real-world road risk.
alt: Generated synthetic accidents, seed 399. Counts lack traffic exposure and reporting denominators, so they do not establish real-world road risk.
question: Does the highest casualty count identify the most dangerous region?
answer: No. Exposure and reporting coverage must be considered.

title: Same data, different visual questions
caption: Synthetic values: North=40, South=20, East=30, West=10 USD. Regions have no natural continuous order; a connecting line can imply one.
alt: Synthetic values: North=40, South=20, East=30, West=10 USD. Regions have no natural continuous order; a connecting line can imply one.
question: Which chart best compares regional revenue?
answer: A bar chart with an appropriate order.

title: Make the comparison easier to read
caption: Same synthetic values in both panels. The improved chart uses a zero baseline, ranking, units, and a focused title.
alt: Same synthetic values in both panels. The improved chart uses a zero baseline, ranking, units, and a focused title.
question: Why is the zero baseline important for bars?
answer: Bar length encodes magnitude; truncation distorts that comparison.

title: Advanced forms for specific questions
caption: Synthetic examples. A waterfall reconciles signed contributions. Funnel stages describe the same defined cohort; stage conversion and overall conversion differ.
alt: Synthetic examples. A waterfall reconciles signed contributions. Funnel stages describe the same defined cohort; stage conversion and overall conversion differ.
question: What is overall purchase conversion?

title: Shared scales support comparison
caption: Synthetic six-month regional revenue. All panels use 0–25 USD, so vertical positions are comparable.
alt: Synthetic six-month regional revenue. All panels use 0–25 USD, so vertical positions are comparable.
question: How would independent y-scales change the impression?
answer: They can hide differences in level even while showing each trend clearly.

title: A dashboard organized around a decision
caption: Conceptual wireframe, not a software screenshot. KPI definitions and filter context make numbers interpretable.
alt: Conceptual wireframe, not a software screenshot. KPI definitions and filter context make numbers interpretable.
question: Why show filter context?
answer: The same measure changes under different dates and segments.

title: Power Query: shape before loading
caption: Conceptual workflow, not a fabricated Power BI screenshot. The lab supplies exact Desktop steps.
alt: Conceptual workflow, not a fabricated Power BI screenshot. The lab supplies exact Desktop steps.
question: How does append differ from merge?
answer: Append adds rows; merge joins columns by keys.

title: Report interactions have distinct purposes
caption: A report and a Power BI Service dashboard are different objects. The bundled HTML report is a teaching implementation, not Power BI UI.
alt: A report and a Power BI Service dashboard are different objects. The bundled HTML report is a teaching implementation, not Power BI UI.
question: Does a screenshot demonstrate filter behavior?
answer: No; test the interactive report.

title: Order-line star schema
caption: Dimension keys are unique. Sales contains one order line; distinct orders differ from row count.
alt: Four dimensions connect with one-to-many dimension-to-fact arrows to Sales.
question: Can OrderID be the unique key of this fact?
answer: No; orders can have multiple lines. Use OrderID plus LineID.

title: Row context and filter context
caption: Synthetic example. COUNTROWS measures lines; DISTINCTCOUNT(OrderID) measures orders.
alt: Synthetic example. COUNTROWS measures lines; DISTINCTCOUNT(OrderID) measures orders.
question: What is AOV if you divide total by four lines?
answer: 125 USD is average line revenue, not average order value.

title: Date sets control time intelligence
caption: Classic date-column patterns require a suitable calendar and relationship. A missing prior-year fact period may correctly return BLANK.
alt: Classic date-column patterns require a suitable calendar and relationship. A missing prior-year fact period may correctly return BLANK.
question: Why remove the whole date table for full-history totals?
answer: A remaining Year/Month filter could constrain the cumulative date set.

title: Measure performance; do not invent improvements
caption: Procedure, not fabricated benchmark results. Native Power BI measurements must be supplied by executing Desktop.
alt: Procedure, not fabricated benchmark results. Native Power BI measurements must be supplied by executing Desktop.
question: Does hiding a column reduce model storage?
answer: No; removing a stored column can.

title: Dashboard project acceptance criteria
caption: The bundled interactive HTML report demonstrates concepts; a Power BI submission still requires a .pbix built in Desktop.
alt: The bundled interactive HTML report demonstrates concepts; a Power BI submission still requires a .pbix built in Desktop.
question: What proves the dashboard total is correct?
answer: Reconcile it to source/Python reference totals under identical filters.

title: Ethics at every project stage
caption: Risk review is continuous. Synthetic teaching data avoids exposing patient or customer identities.
alt: Risk review is continuous. Synthetic teaching data avoids exposing patient or customer identities.
question: Does hashing guarantee anonymous data?
answer: No; linkage and re-identification can remain possible.

title: Capstone proposal canvas
caption: Proposal criteria are course guidance, not a claim of institutional assessment policy.
alt: Proposal criteria are course guidance, not a claim of institutional assessment policy.
question: What makes a proposal feasible?
answer: A bounded question, accessible data, realistic methods and explicit acceptance criteria.

title: Capstone lab checkpoints
caption: A surprising finding is not mandatory: honest, reproducible evidence is more valuable than a dramatic narrative.
alt: A surprising finding is not mandatory: honest, reproducible evidence is more valuable than a dramatic narrative.
question: What if the EDA contradicts the proposal hypothesis?
answer: Report it honestly and revise the interpretation.

title: Final dashboard quality checks
caption: Example failures: multiplied join rows, order-line counts mislabeled as orders, stale refresh, or inaccessible color-only status.
alt: Example failures: multiplied join rows, order-line counts mislabeled as orders, stale refresh, or inaccessible color-only status.
question: How can a plausible number still be wrong?
answer: Incorrect grain, joins or filter context can produce believable but invalid totals.

title: Presentation: evidence to decision
caption: Use associated with for observational findings. Reserve causal claims for appropriate designs and assumptions.
alt: Use associated with for observational findings. Reserve causal claims for appropriate designs and assumptions.
question: What belongs next to the recommendation?
answer: Its evidence, limits, and an evaluation plan.
